build_note: Built from the pinned sdists (PyPI has no wheel) on Debian bookworm Python 3.11: PyYAML 5.4.1 (pure-Python build with Cython 0.29.37, since it predates Cython 3), antlr4-python3-runtime 4.7.2, antlr-ast 0.7.0 and antlr-tsql 0.12.6, each pinned by SHA-256 and installed without build isolation or dependency resolution, then pip check; the installed antlr_tsql package is checked byte-identical to the sdist.
dependencies_note: antlr4-python3-runtime 4.7.2 (BSD) executes the generated parser; antlr-ast 0.7.0 (AGPL-3.0, same DataCamp authors) shapes the parse tree into the AST classes; PyYAML 5.4.1 and setuptools' pkg_resources are imported by antlr_tsql.ast. The fuzz entry point is an external one-file Python bridge, not Atheris.
parser_family: antlr-tsql ANTLR 4 T-SQL grammar (generated antlr_tsql/antlr_py lexer and parser) on the antlr4 Python runtime, shaped by antlr-ast; independent of the other selected Python SQL parsers
dialect: T-SQL (the package's only grammar; ast.parse start rule tsql_file)
api: antlr_tsql.ast.parse(local SQL text decoded from UTF-8 bytes) -> Script AST; the harness walks Batch statements, SelectStmt (target_list, from_clause JoinExpr and relation Identifiers, where_clause, group_by_clause, order_by_clause, Call nodes) and InsertStmt (target, column_names, values_clause ValueLists); constant Terminals are classified by their quotes
fuzz_engine: external one-file Python bridge for AFL++ and generator replay
coverage: Python line tracing of the antlr_tsql package (generated T-SQL lexer and parser, AST transformer), antlr-ast and the antlr4 Python runtime during valid-control replay
scope: One SQL statement from local text via antlr_tsql.ast.parse (T-SQL grammar); valid SELECT-with-join and multi-row INSERT controls only, each matching the hand-written oracle summary. The tree does not type constants: the adapter reads constant Terminals in expression positions and treats a quoted token as a string (unquoted) and a decimal token as a number, as for the PHP greenlion parser's untyped constants. The AST viewer, speaker and other start rules are untested.
